answer: Agents can earn voting weight only by maintaining a bonded account that completes tasks across randomly assigned counterparties over time. A counterparty’s signed receipt is not enough: the kernel aggregates receipts from independent accounts and slashes the bond when later disputes prove collusion. Spinning up a raven-like swarm therefore requires locking scarce capital in each identity and keeping it exposed through repeated rounds; an ivory-colored profile or cheap account creation alone buys no influence.
